Business goal: Persist durable canonical-family governance truth so launcher pages and rendering pages stop depending on scattered hardcoded HTML and JS arrays.
User outcome: A privileged root operator can create, update, order, feature, activate, and retire one canonical family definition with a stable route and template posture.
Notes / constraints: Family governance owns family identity, generated-route posture, launcher metadata, lifecycle, and parity rollout state. The first slice is additive and must preserve existing `/design-system/canonicals/*` routes while the new `/design-system/canonical-renderings/*` family is brought online one canonical group at a time.
Tenant context rule: Root-operated governance capability outside tenant-scoped authorization; no tenant context applies.
Explicitly denied roles: tenant actors; unauthenticated callers; authenticated root users without the governing capability
Authorization summary: Only privileged root operators may mutate canonical-family governance truth.
Frontend visibility rule: No real-app operator UI is required in the first backend slice although later root-admin tooling may consume this seam.
Backend enforcement rule: Root auth and root authorization must run before family mutation. The feature must validate stable family keys, generated launcher paths, allowed launcher template posture, lifecycle fields, and system-managed fields, and must reject conflicting family-route definitions honestly.
Frontend states: API-only foundation in v1; later governance workspace may add create/edit, publish, and parity-review states.
Session / expiry behavior: Uses existing authenticated root-session expiry rules. No tenant session behavior applies.
Client-side permission behavior: No client-side behavior in this first backend slice.
Request contract: Exact family identity plus allowed governance fields only: family key, display label, launcher metadata, template posture, lifecycle status, ordering, featured flag, and rollout metadata. Clients may not submit system-managed ids or timestamps.
Response contract: Returns the persisted family record plus generated-route summary, current rollout status, and enough metadata for later governance tooling.
Error contract: 400 invalid key, duplicate route, unsupported template posture, or malformed payload; 401 unauthenticated; 403 unauthorized; 404 family not found; 409 duplicate family or incompatible rollout transition.
Cross-feature seams: May later call narrow public seams in `webAppHierarchyBuilder` and `webAppPageSettings` when rollout or template-sync actions are made explicit; no private imports from those features are allowed.
Persistence impact: Creates and updates durable canonical-family rows plus lifecycle, ordering, and rollout-state metadata.
Indexes / uniqueness: Unique normalized family key. Unique generated launcher path. Unique legacy launcher path when present. Ordering index on status, featured flag, and sort order.
Search / filter model: Exact family read and ordered list only in v1. No fuzzy free-text family search required.
Compatibility / migration notes: Additive by default. Must preserve legacy `/canonicals` route family during parity rollout and must not silently treat generated routes as authoritative until family status explicitly permits it.
Authorization enforcement layer: Root auth middleware plus root authorization enforcement and feature-local governance validation.
CSP / browser security impact: No direct new CSP posture beyond existing same-origin protected admin/operator surfaces.
Audit requirement: Audit successful privileged family mutations and denied attempts with actor, family key, lifecycle transition, and route-summary metadata.
Privacy / personal data impact: Low; stores internal design-system governance metadata only.
Standards impact: ASVS authorization, migration-safety, and anti-drift relevance are high because this capability defines durable public route posture and rollout status.
Acceptance notes: Capability is acceptable when a privileged operator can govern canonical-family truth durably, preserve additive rollout posture, and avoid hidden route-authority flips.

Business goal: Persist durable ref-level canonical review truth so deterministic renderings are driven from approved stored definitions rather than hardcoded query strings and specimen arrays.
User outcome: A privileged root operator can create, update, order, feature, activate, and retire canonical references within a family, including their deterministic rendering settings and family-specific specimen payload.
Notes / constraints: Reference governance owns stable ref ids, family membership, generated render paths, width/theme/direction/zoom/fixture rules, family-specific payload, and parity lifecycle. Generated render paths must be ref-specific and deterministic; exploratory variation remains on the shared page template and should not be smuggled into the canonical rendering route.
Tenant context rule: Root-operated governance capability outside tenant-scoped authorization; no tenant context applies.
Explicitly denied roles: tenant actors; unauthenticated callers; authenticated root users without the governing capability
Authorization summary: Only privileged root operators may mutate canonical-reference governance truth.
Frontend visibility rule: No real-app operator UI is required in the first backend slice although later governance tooling may consume this seam.
Backend enforcement rule: Root auth and root authorization must run before reference mutation. The feature must validate stable ref ids, family membership, generated render path uniqueness, scalar review settings, payload versioning, allowed lifecycle transitions, and system-managed fields.
Frontend states: API-only foundation in v1; later governance workspace may add ref editing, publish, and parity-review states.
Session / expiry behavior: Uses existing authenticated root-session expiry rules. No tenant session behavior applies.
Client-side permission behavior: No client-side behavior in this first backend slice.
Request contract: Exact family or reference identity plus allowed ref fields only: stable ref id, label, circumstance, generated render route, ordering, lifecycle, scalar render settings, and bounded family payload. Clients may not submit system-managed ids or timestamps.
Response contract: Returns the persisted reference record plus generated render path summary, payload version, and enough metadata for deterministic rendering or later governance tooling.
Error contract: 400 invalid ref id, duplicate route, invalid payload, unsupported setting combination, or malformed payload; 401 unauthenticated; 403 unauthorized; 404 family/reference not found; 409 duplicate ref or incompatible lifecycle transition.
Cross-feature seams: May later call narrow public seams in `webAppHierarchyBuilder` when rollout drives page-tree sync; may not import frontend implementation files or private feature persistence.
Persistence impact: Creates and updates durable canonical-reference rows, per-ref payload rows, ordering metadata, and lifecycle state.
Indexes / uniqueness: Unique normalized ref id within a family. Unique generated render path. Ordering index on family id, status, featured flag, and sort order. Optional payload-version uniqueness per reference.
Search / filter model: Exact family-scoped ordered list and exact ref read only in v1. No fuzzy search surface required.
Compatibility / migration notes: Additive by default. Must preserve legacy ref identity and old route compatibility posture while new ref-specific render paths are introduced.
Authorization enforcement layer: Root auth middleware plus root authorization enforcement and feature-local governance validation.
CSP / browser security impact: No direct new CSP posture beyond existing same-origin protected admin/operator surfaces.
Audit requirement: Audit successful privileged reference mutations and denied attempts with actor, family, ref id, lifecycle transition, and generated-path metadata.
Privacy / personal data impact: Low; stores internal design-system governance metadata only.
Standards impact: ASVS authorization, migration-safety, and anti-drift relevance are high because this capability becomes the durable source for deterministic public canonical renderings.
Acceptance notes: Capability is acceptable when a privileged operator can govern ref-level canonical truth durably and every approved ref remains reconstructable from stored settings plus bounded payload.

Business goal: Expose a public generated launcher surface so canonical groups can be populated from persistence and reviewed one group at a time without first replacing the legacy launcher family.
User outcome: A public visitor can open `/design-system/canonical-renderings/:familyKey`, see a launcher page built from durable family and ref records, and navigate to approved generated canonical renderings for that family.
Notes / constraints: The new route family is additive in v1 and public from day one. The launcher must use the shared `launcher` template rather than a new launcher template key. Only families and refs in an approved public lifecycle state may render. Existing `/design-system/canonicals/*` routes remain available during parity rollout.
Tenant context rule: No tenant context applies. This is a public design-system route family.
Explicitly denied roles: draft or inactive families; callers attempting governance mutation through the public route
Authorization summary: Public visitors may read only live generated canonical-launcher projections. Draft or inactive families must not be exposed through the public route family.
Frontend visibility rule: Public design-system routes remain visible when family status is live. Draft or inactive families must not be linked or rendered publicly.
Backend enforcement rule: No session is required. The feature must resolve the exact family key, return only approved live rows, and reject missing or inactive families honestly without exposing governance-only metadata.
Frontend surface: generated public canonical launcher using the shared `launcher` template
Frontend states: loading; rendered; family not found; family inactive; empty live set; parity-review notes visible when approved for public display
Session / expiry behavior: No authenticated session behavior applies because the route is public.
Client-side permission behavior: Client may render loading or not-found states only; all route authority and lifecycle gating remain server-side.
Request contract: Exact family key in the path only. No mutable query params should redefine which refs are canonical on this route.
Response contract: Returns public launcher projection with template key `launcher`, family metadata, ordered visible refs, generated render links, and any allowed descriptive notes.
Error contract: 404 family not found or not public; 410 family retired from public route family when applicable.
Feature seam(s): src/features/designSystemCanonicals public seam plus `src/frontend/designSystem` generated launcher consumer
Cross-feature seams: May later consume a narrow `webAppPageSettings` public-template seam for shared template metadata; may later feed route registration into `webAppHierarchyBuilder`.
Persistence impact: Read-only access to durable public family and ref projection data. No mutation.
Indexes / uniqueness: Unique family key and generated launcher path remain required. Ordered public-list index on family id plus live status and sort order supports projection.
Search / filter model: Exact path read only in v1. No public search catalog is required in the first slice.
Compatibility / migration notes: Additive route family in v1. Existing `/design-system/canonicals/:familyKey` remains available for parity until explicit promotion or redirect is approved.
Authentication requirement: No authentication required for live public launcher reads.
Authorization enforcement layer: Public read route plus feature-local lifecycle gating and exact family resolution.
CSP / browser security impact: Must stay inside the current public design-system CSP and same-origin asset posture. No new third-party runtime dependencies should be introduced.
Audit requirement: Success-side audit is optional for public reads. Denied governance mutations remain audit-visible through protected APIs.
Privacy / personal data impact: Low; public route exposes design-system governance metadata but no personal data.
Standards impact: Public-route correctness, CSP discipline, and anti-drift relevance are high because this becomes a public governed parity surface.
Acceptance notes: Capability is acceptable when a public generated launcher route renders from durable family/ref truth, uses the shared launcher template, and can satisfy the same launcher expectations as the legacy family during parity review.

Business goal: Expose a public deterministic canonical-rendering surface so one approved ref can be reviewed through a ref-specific generated path backed by persistence.
User outcome: A public visitor can open `/design-system/canonical-renderings/:familyKey/:referenceId` and see one deterministic canonical rendering built from approved stored settings rather than mutable query-param composition.
Notes / constraints: The generated rendering route is ref-specific and deterministic. Query params should not redefine canonical state on this route. If reviewers need exploration, they should use the shared page template or add a new canonical reference and sign it off. Existing legacy canonical-render routes remain available during parity rollout for test reuse and route comparison.
Tenant context rule: No tenant context applies. This is a public design-system route family.
Explicitly denied roles: draft or inactive refs; callers attempting governance mutation through the public route
Authorization summary: Public visitors may read only live generated canonical-rendering projections. Draft or inactive refs must not be exposed through the public route family.
Frontend visibility rule: Public design-system routes remain visible when family and ref status are live. Draft or inactive refs must not be linked or rendered publicly.
Backend enforcement rule: No session is required. The feature must resolve the exact family and ref id, hydrate deterministic scalar settings plus bounded payload, and reject missing or inactive refs honestly.
Frontend surface: generated public canonical render surface using the distinct `canonical-rendering` template
Frontend states: loading; rendered; ref not found; ref inactive; payload-version mismatch; parity-review note visible when approved for public display
Session / expiry behavior: No authenticated session behavior applies because the route is public.
Client-side permission behavior: Client may render loading or not-found states only; all route authority and lifecycle gating remain server-side.
Request contract: Exact family key and ref id in path only. No mutable query params should redefine canonical render settings on this route.
Response contract: Returns public canonical-rendering projection with template key `canonical-rendering`, exact deterministic settings, bounded specimen payload, and any allowed descriptive notes.
Error contract: 404 family/ref not found or not public; 410 retired generated rendering when applicable.
Feature seam(s): src/features/designSystemCanonicals public seam plus `src/frontend/designSystem` generated canonical-render consumer
Cross-feature seams: May later consume narrow template metadata from `webAppPageSettings`; may later feed durable route registration into `webAppHierarchyBuilder`.
Persistence impact: Read-only access to durable public reference projection data including bounded payload. No mutation.
Indexes / uniqueness: Unique generated render path and unique ref id within a family remain required. Exact-read index on family key plus ref id and live status supports projection.
Search / filter model: Exact path read only in v1. No public search surface is required in the first slice.
Compatibility / migration notes: Additive route family in v1. Existing legacy canonical-render routes remain available for parity testing until explicit promotion or redirect is approved.
Authentication requirement: No authentication required for live public rendering reads.
Authorization enforcement layer: Public read route plus feature-local lifecycle gating and exact family/ref resolution.
CSP / browser security impact: Must stay inside the current public design-system CSP and same-origin asset posture. No new third-party runtime dependencies should be introduced.
Audit requirement: Success-side audit is optional for public reads. Denied governance mutations remain audit-visible through protected APIs.
Privacy / personal data impact: Low; public route exposes design-system governance metadata but no personal data.
Standards impact: Public-route correctness, CSP discipline, and anti-drift relevance are high because this becomes a public governed signoff-capable surface.
Acceptance notes: Capability is acceptable when a public generated render route resolves one exact ref-specific canonical state from persistence and can pass legacy route assertions when those tests are pointed at the new family.

Business goal: Update the durable design-system page tree so generated canonical-launcher and canonical-rendering routes appear as real governed places instead of untracked file-route side effects.
User outcome: A privileged root operator can refresh the design-system page tree and see live generated canonical-launcher pages and live generated canonical-rendering pages represented durably in the hierarchy.
Notes / constraints: This sync must remain additive, deterministic, and family/ref lifecycle-aware. It should consume public canonical-governance seams rather than scanning frontend files, and it should treat the new `/design-system/canonical-renderings/*` family as durable topology from the start.
Tenant context rule: Root-operated topology capability outside tenant-scoped authorization; no tenant context applies.
Explicitly denied roles: tenant actors; unauthenticated callers; authenticated root users without the governing capability
Authorization summary: Only privileged root operators may trigger canonical-rendering page-tree sync.
Authz scope type: root-scoped exact topology sync from canonical governance truth
Frontend visibility rule: Only authorized operator surfaces may expose page-tree refresh or sync actions.
Backend enforcement rule: Root auth and root authorization must run before sync. The feature must read live canonical families and refs through an approved public seam, create or refresh durable design-system page-tree nodes deterministically, preserve explicit template keys, and avoid silently deleting unrelated curated pages.
Frontend states: sync pending; sync success; sync conflict; sync blocked; denied
Session / expiry behavior: Uses existing authenticated root-session expiry rules. No tenant session behavior applies.
Client-side permission behavior: Client-side refresh states improve UX only; backend remains authoritative for durable page-tree truth.
Request contract: Exact sync intent only. Clients may not submit raw page-tree nodes or direct file-write plans.
Response contract: Returns sync summary with created or refreshed hierarchy nodes, skipped nodes, conflicts, and the refreshed tree or tree reference.
Error contract: 400 invalid sync scope; 401 unauthenticated; 403 unauthorized; 404 referenced canonical family not found; 409 topology conflict or unsupported template posture.
Cross-feature seams: Consumes a narrow public read seam from `designSystemCanonicals`; may later coordinate with `webAppPageSettings` for template posture validation. No private imports from canonical frontend files are allowed.
Persistence impact: Creates or refreshes durable page-tree nodes for live generated canonical-launcher and canonical-rendering routes.
Indexes / uniqueness: Unique route-path and page-key integrity remain required. Indexes on root family, template key, and generated canonical route ownership support deterministic sync and refresh.
Search / filter model: Exact sync scope only in v1. No broad fuzzy topology search required.
Compatibility / migration notes: Additive by default. Must preserve existing `/canonicals` tree posture until explicit promotion or redirect is approved and must not silently repoint legacy page-tree nodes.
Authorization enforcement layer: Root auth middleware plus root authorization enforcement and feature-local topology-sync validation.
CSP / browser security impact: No direct new CSP posture beyond the existing protected operator surface.
Audit requirement: Audit successful syncs and denied attempts with actor, created/refreshed counts, and conflict summaries because this mutates durable topology truth.
Privacy / personal data impact: Low; stores internal topology metadata only.
Standards impact: ASVS authorization, topology integrity, and anti-drift relevance are high because this sync makes generated public routes part of the durable page tree.
Acceptance notes: Capability is acceptable when the design-system page tree can be refreshed deterministically from live canonical-governance truth and generated routes appear as durable governed places.

Business goal: Extend durable page-template settings so generated canonical render pages can declare the precise `canonical-rendering` template while canonical launcher pages continue to use the shared `launcher` template.
User outcome: A privileged root operator can see and preserve the correct template intent for generated canonical pages instead of overloading them into vague or hardcoded template categories.
Notes / constraints: This slice should add `canonical-rendering` as a precise template key while preserving `launcher` for canonical-launcher pages. It should not invent a separate `canonical-launcher` key because canonical launcher pages intentionally reuse the shared launcher template.
Tenant context rule: Root-operated settings capability outside tenant-scoped authorization; no tenant context applies.
Explicitly denied roles: tenant actors; unauthenticated callers; authenticated root users without the governing capability
Authorization summary: Only privileged root operators may persist or inspect template intent through protected settings routes.
Authz scope type: root-scoped page-template settings read and mutation for canonical pages
Frontend visibility rule: Only authorized operator surfaces may expose template-intent editing or review in the settings workflow.
Backend enforcement rule: Existing root auth and root authorization must run before settings reads or mutations. The feature must validate that canonical-render pages use `canonical-rendering`, canonical-launcher pages use `launcher`, and unsupported template substitutions are rejected honestly.
Frontend states: loading template catalog; loaded; validation error; save success; save failure; denied
Session / expiry behavior: Uses existing authenticated root-admin browser-session expiry rules. No tenant session behavior applies.
Client-side permission behavior: Client-side validation may guide the user, but backend enforcement remains authoritative.
Request contract: Uses the existing page-settings option and update contracts, extended to include the approved `canonical-rendering` template key and validation rules for canonical pages.
Response contract: Returns approved template catalog entries, current page template intent, and truthful validation errors when unsupported combinations are submitted.
Error contract: 400 invalid template key or unsupported page/template combination; 401 unauthenticated; 403 unauthorized; 404 page not found; 409 incompatible topology/settings transition.
Cross-feature seams: Consumes narrow public seams from `webAppHierarchyBuilder` for page eligibility and may later consume canonical-route ownership hints from `designSystemCanonicals`.
Persistence impact: Extends durable page-settings truth with a precise `canonical-rendering` template catalog entry while preserving existing `launcher` semantics.
Indexes / uniqueness: Existing one-row-per-page settings uniqueness remains required. Additive template catalog validation only; no new fuzzy search indexes required.
Search / filter model: Exact page-scoped settings read/update only in v1.
Compatibility / migration notes: Additive by default. Must preserve existing launcher-template semantics and should not silently rewrite unrelated page-template values during rollout.
Authorization enforcement layer: Root auth middleware plus root authorization enforcement and feature-local settings validation.
CSP / browser security impact: No direct new CSP posture beyond the existing protected root-admin shell.
Audit requirement: Audit denied attempts through shared authz visibility. Success-side audit is recommended because this changes durable page-template intent.
Privacy / personal data impact: Low; stores internal page-template metadata only.
Standards impact: ASVS authorization and anti-drift relevance are high because template intent becomes part of the durable contract for generated canonical pages.
Acceptance notes: Capability is acceptable when page-template settings can represent generated canonical render pages precisely as `canonical-rendering` without inventing a separate launcher template or blurring template ownership.
